subject: Compiler directives
notes: kb/Work PB1361 (w70b): '2) A compiler directive shall be preceded only by zero, one, or more space characters.' (cite.py --check 7.3.3 -> OK §7.3.3 2)). CompilerDirectiveLine.TryParse has ONE reading (only spaces/tab before >>); the allowSequenceArea 'digits or spaces' mode is deleted. The reference-format stage hands it the program-text area of the format in effect (DirectiveText: positions 8 to margin R of a source line in fixed form, §7.3.3 SR3 'When the reference format is fixed-form, a compiler directive shall be written in the program-text area' -> OK §7.3.3 3); the whole line in free form), so '       12 >>SOURCE FORMAT FREE' (fixed) and '000100 >>SOURCE FORMAT FIXED' (free) are program text, not switches, and are rejected (COBOL0001); the post-normalization stages already held the same reading. retired-witness: unit:ReferenceFormatLogicalConversionTests.FreeFormLine_WithTextBeforeTheIndicator_IsNotADirective (kb/Work PB1690: the test now also pins the named diagnostic COBOL2691 and is renamed FreeFormLine_WithTextBeforeTheIndicator_IsNotADirective_AndIsDiagnosed)
